text:
devon: Heads-up — getting an APAC customer escalation about increased p95/p99 latency on the /v1/generate endpoint since ~07:40 UTC. They report big TLS handshake times (~200-400ms extra) and occasional 524s timeouts.

matt: Link to the latency dashboard?

devon: https://console.redwood.internal/d/latency/edge-p95?from=now-1h to=now — spike starts ~07:38 UTC, p95 went from 120ms -> 480ms. p99 up to ~1.2s. Mostly APAC -> EU routing.

ops-bot: Alert: APAC-edge tls_handshake_duration.p95 > 300ms for 7m. affected services: api/text-gen, api/chat. incident_id=INC-2026-342

jia: quick repro from Tokyo (home lab):
```
$ time curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer x..." -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
* TLS handshake completed in 0.45s
* Connected to api.redwood.ai (203.0.113.45) port 443 (#0)
> POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
real    0m0.63s
```

net-bot: traceroute from apac-pop-3 -> api.redwood.ai showing extra hop through eu-agg-1 since 07:35:
```
1  apac-pop-3 10.0.1.1
2  isp-nap-2 203.0.113.1
3  eu-agg-1 52.95.20.14  <-- unexpected hop
4  api-edge-eu 52.95.20.200
```

sara: we rolled a geo-fanout policy change at 07:30 to prefer EU nodes for low-util APAC traffic (experiment 4212). It was meant to improve cache hit rates but could cause hairpins.

matt: That aligns. If TLS handshake now crosses AZs/regions, extra RTT adds up. Any recent DNS TTL changes?

jia: DNS lookup shows short TTL (30s) for api.redwood.ai during repro.

support-bot: Customer ticket TCK-8853: complaining about intermittent 5xx and slow responses. Provided logs and curl traces.

devon: Repro steps for SRE to validate:
1) From an APAC test instance: curl -w '%{time_appconnect} %{time_connect} %{time_total}\n' -o /dev/null -s https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
2) dig +short api.redwood.ai @<local-resolver>
3) traceroute -n api.redwood.ai

matt: Quick mitigation idea: roll back geo-fanout policy to previous selector (old: prefer local-pop). Also bump DNS TTL to 300s to avoid rapid flapping while we debug. Can we do a targeted rollback?

sara: Yes — I can push rollback to canary and route APAC back to apac-pop-1/2 only. Doing canary now.

ops-bot: Deploy started: rollout/geo-policy/4212 -> rollback(canary). 2/2 canary nodes updated.

net-bot: Preliminary telemetry after canary rollback: apac p95 dropped from 480ms -> 160ms within 90s. TLS handshake p95 down to ~110ms.

devon: Good. Keep rollback for now. We'll run a deeper root-cause: why did geo-fanout prefer EU? Hypothesis: health check false-positive on APAC edge causing traffic to be steered.

jia: I'll collect tcpdumps on apac-pop-1 for 10m and post PCAP to artifacts. Also collecting SNI/ClientHello times.

matt: Also correlate with recent peering flaps with ISP partner NAP-2 (ticket NET-2119). Could be transient BGP reroute causing path to eu-agg-1.

devon: Action items:
- sara: keep canary rollback for 1h and monitor p95/p99 (ops-bot: auto-alert if >200ms for >5m).
- jia: upload pcaps + curl traces to INC-2026-342 folder.
- net team: sanity-check BGP/peering logs for 07:20-07:40 window.
- matt: open postmortem template after incident stabilizes.

support-bot: Customer updated: "Thanks — latency improved after your change. We'll watch for regressions." :thumbsup:

sara: I'll follow up with a safe re-roll plan: add health-checks (sni+tls) and prefer locality more strongly; also add a fallback rule to avoid eu fanout if tls_handshake_duration > 200ms.

devon: Thanks all. We'll keep thread open for postmortem notes. If anyone sees p95 creep after rollback, ping @devon directly. :eyes:
